definitions.value_direction: Higher values are generally associated with greater Alzheimer's-related tau pathology; assay-specific interpretation and validation are mandatory.
limitations: This is a pathology-associated analyte and not a direct measurement of latent progression velocity dP/dt.
Performance, units, cutoffs and calibration are assay- and population-dependent; platform identity must be retained.
A plasma p-tau217 value does not measure total proteostasis capacity or the full tau-processing system.

definitions.value_direction: Lower ratios are generally associated with cerebral amyloid pathology; interpretation requires assay- and protocol-specific calibration.
limitations: Aβ42/40 is a pathology-associated ratio and is not a direct measurement of progression velocity.
Absolute concentrations and ratios are not interchangeable; retain raw analyte values and the versioned ratio calculation when available.
CSF collection, processing, storage, assay platform and batch effects must be retained.

definitions.value_direction: Higher values may indicate greater astrocytic activation or response; they do not represent the complete neuroinflammatory state.
limitations: GFAP is an astrocytic-response proxy and is not a complete measure of microglial, cytokine, complement or CNS immune activity.
Peripheral GFAP does not directly quantify regional CNS inflammatory activity.
Interpretation depends on assay platform, specimen handling and relevant comorbidities.

definitions.value_direction: Higher values indicate greater neuroaxonal injury signal but are not specific to Alzheimer's disease.
limitations: NfL is an injury/turnover marker and not a direct measurement of preserved neuronal integrity.
NfL is not disease-specific and may reflect injury from multiple neurological or systemic processes.
A value must not be interpreted without assay, specimen, age/context and collection metadata.

definitions.analyte_or_metric: regional fluorodeoxyglucose PET standardized uptake value ratio
definitions.value_direction: Lower regional FDG uptake may indicate regional glucose hypometabolism; direction depends on region, reference region and processing pipeline.
limitations: FDG-PET reflects regional glucose utilization and is not a direct measurement of ATP concentration, oxidative phosphorylation or total metabolic health.
SUVR is dependent on reference region, acquisition timing, reconstruction, scanner and processing pipeline.
A regional imaging metric is not equivalent to a global scalar metabolic state.

definitions.value_direction: Higher Centiloid values indicate greater amyloid PET signal under the specified tracer and validated conversion pipeline.
limitations: Centiloid values require validated tracer-specific conversion and a specified processing pipeline.
Amyloid PET is a pathological biomarker and is not a direct measure of latent progression velocity or current cognitive function.
Amyloid PET staging and fluid-biomarker staging are not interchangeable without validated bridging.

definitions.value_direction: Lower hippocampal volume may indicate regional atrophy; it is an indirect morphometric measure and not a neuronal cell count.
limitations: MRI-derived regional volume depends on acquisition, scanner, sequence, segmentation software and quality control.
Volume is a tissue-level morphometric observation and is not a direct measurement of neuronal viability or synaptic function.
Intracranial-volume adjustment and longitudinal scanner harmonization must be declared and versioned.

definitions.analyte_or_metric: Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale cognitive subscale total score
definitions.value_direction: Higher scores indicate greater measured cognitive impairment; reverse-direction interpretation is required when modelling functional capacity Q.
limitations: A cognitive scale measures one phenotype domain and is not a direct measurement of neuronal integrity or the full functional-capacity construct.
Versions, language, assessor procedures, education and practice effects may affect comparability.
The score direction is impairment-oriented and must not be mistaken for the positive polarity of Q.

definitions.analyte_or_metric: CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay result
definitions.value_direction: Positive indicates detectable alpha-synuclein seeding activity under the specified assay protocol; negative does not exclude every Parkinson-related pathology or subtype.
limitations: A seed-amplification assay detects seeding activity for the assay substrate and protocol; it does not quantify total proteostasis capacity, autophagic flux or all alpha-synuclein species.
Assay performance and interpretation vary with synucleinopathy subtype, specimen, protocol and cohort; a negative result does not define absence of every disease mechanism.
Protocols and preanalytical factors require standardization and version tracking.

definitions.value_direction: Higher scores indicate greater motor impairment; reverse-direction interpretation is required when modelling functional capacity Q.
limitations: Part III is a motor examination and does not represent all non-motor function or activities of daily living.
Medication state, assessor training, instrument version and visit protocol influence comparability.
The score is impairment-oriented and must not be mapped directly to the positively oriented Q latent state.
